name: Subject Tracking And Statement Zoom
use_when: A short-form talking-head clip needs more energy while keeping the speaker centered.
The speaker moves and the crop needs manual tracking.
Important statements need visual emphasis through zoom-ins or zoom-outs.
A moving subject or background action needs manual CapCut-style keyframes to stay centered.
CapCut automatic face/body/hand tracking can keep a subject framed when the tracked feature remains visible.
avoid_when: The speaker is already stable and centered.
The crop would cut off hands, body language, captions, or important props.
The statement is not important enough to deserve motion emphasis.
The subject turns away, leaves frame, or becomes occluded enough that automatic tracking will drift.

timeline_pattern.pattern: body_room_frame -> center_guides -> position_keyframe -> re_center_during_movement -> statement_zoom -> hold_or_cut
timeline_pattern.framing_rule: Leave room around the body during filming or crop selection so zooms and tracking have space.
timeline_pattern.tracking_rule: Use center guides and position keyframes to keep the subject aligned through movement.
timeline_pattern.manual_tracking_rule: For manual tracking, add new position keyframes at movement turns or every few frames while the subject changes direction or speed.
timeline_pattern.auto_tracking_rule: Use built-in face/body/hand tracking only when the target stays visible; shorten the range or fall back to manual keyframes when the tracker loses the feature.
timeline_pattern.zoom_rule: Use zooms to highlight important statements; use tracking to follow movement.

motion.rule: Animate scale and position together so the subject remains centered and readable.

keyframe_values.statement_zoom_scale: Start around 108-125% for social emphasis; go larger only when the crop still preserves face, hands, and captions.
keyframe_values.tracking_keyframe_spacing: Add position keyframes every 4-12 frames during visible movement, or only at movement turns when the motion is slow.
keyframe_values.center_tolerance: Keep the speaker's face or chest near the vertical center guide unless composition intentionally favors text or proof.
keyframe_values.hold_after_zoom: Hold 8-18 frames after the zoom lands so the emphasis registers.
keyframe_values.auto_tracking_target: Choose face, body, or hand based on which feature remains visible through the full tracking range.

sound.rule: Use a subtle whoosh or hit only when the zoom is meant to be felt; keep speech clear.

captions.rule: Caption safe area must be checked after every crop or tracking move.

color.rule: No direct color rule; avoid zooming into noisy or poorly lit areas that make the speaker look worse.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use crop/scale expressions or zoompan from tracked x/y points. Render a phone-size preview to check body crop and caption safety.
implementation.remotion: Store subjectCenter keyframes and statementBeat frames, then interpolate translate/scale with a hold after emphasis.
implementation.blender: Use camera tracking or an empty target for animated talking-head composites.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use manual keyframes or Camera Tracking on supported devices. Choose face/body/hand target, zoom only as much as needed, keep the chosen subject centered with repeated position adjustments or generated tracking, and preview the vertical crop before export.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Enable rulers/guides, keyframe Position and Scale in Effect Controls, and verify Program Monitor safe margins.

common_mistakes: Cropping so tightly that later zooms cut off the head, hands, or subtitles.
Adding zooms to unimportant filler lines.
Letting the subject drift away from center during movement.
Tracking the face while covering the statement with captions.
Adding too few keyframes so the subject drifts between tracking points.
Adding so many keyframes that the crop jitters instead of following smoothly.
Trusting automatic tracking after the face or target turns out of frame.
qc: Does the speaker stay centered during movement?
Do statement zooms happen only on important lines?
Do zooms preserve face, hands, captions, and proof visuals?
Does the zoom hold long enough to register?
Is the final crop safe at phone size?
Are manual tracking keyframes dense enough to prevent drift but not so dense that they create jitter?
If automatic tracking was used, does the target stay visible and stable through the full range?
